gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured warm-up time: in The Van Conversion's test of Renogy's self-heating 12V 200Ah battery, the cells took about 30 minutes to go from about -2.5°C to about 5°C. During that time the battery took 0 A of charge, then took 20–30 A once warm.
standout_why: I opened three of the four pages ChatGPT cited: BatteryTrail's spec database, CompareFoundry's cold-charging guide and BoondockMaps' best-lithium list. All three say they did no testing and give no heating time, heater draw or measured capacity. BatteryTrail: 'Every figure is a published manufacturer claim.' CompareFoundry: 'We have not independently tested these products.' BoondockMaps: 'We have not lab-tested these units.' The fourth cited page, Gear Ranking, would not load (SSL certificate error), so I couldn't check it. Any measured warm-up or cold-charge figure is new against these pages, but I found one for only one brand, and it's a sister model.
decides: It doesn't pick a winner, because no named reviewer has tested more than one of the candidates. What it does confirm is a buying point: a heater that runs on charger power gives no charge for roughly the first half hour on a cold morning, and needs a few amps of charge current just to start. That favors LiTime LiHeat's pre-heat mode, which can run on the battery itself (a maker claim, not tested), for owners who rely on weak winter solar. The capacity figure for Epoch comes from a non-heated 100Ah unit, so it only weakly supports Epoch's 'best overall' card.

findings.label: Measured warm-up before charging
findings.value: about 30 min from about -2.5°C to about 5°C internal; 0 A charge until warm, then 20–30 A
findings.source_title: Renogy Self-Heating Lithium Battery Review: The Best Battery for Winter Vanlife? (Shane Monks O'Byrne, The Van Conversion)
findings.note: Field use in a van on nights of -5 to -10°C, heated by alternator charge after engine start; temperatures read from Renogy's app. The article also says the temperature climbed 'over the next 15–20 minutes', so call it 'about 30 minutes' at most. The page shows 'Jan 10, updated Apr 5' with no year. Renogy supplied the battery free. This is the 200Ah sibling, not the 100Ah ChatGPT listed. The figure 'about 60–80 W heater (5–6 A)' on the page has no source, so I left it out.

findings.label: Observed heater cut-off and charge time
findings.value: At about 30°F ambient, heater ran until cells reached about 41°F, then charging resumed; about 15% to full in a little over 7 h on a 14.6 V 40 A charger
findings.source_title: Vatrer 12V 300Ah LiFePO4 Lithium Battery Review (2026) – OutdoorCarry (Ash, 2026-10-20)
findings.note: No heater duration was recorded. Arithmetic check: 85% × 300 Ah = 255 Ah; at 40 A that is about 6.4 h, which fits 'a little over seven hours'. Delivered capacity was not measured; 3,840 Wh is Vatrer's rating.

findings.label: Measured capacity, 20-h rundown at 5 A
findings.value: just under 110 Ah new; 108 Ah after high-current abuse tests
findings.source_title: Epoch Batteries, elegant drop-in LiFePO4 (Ben Stein, Panbo, 2023-02-27, updated 2024-02-09)
findings.note: This is not the 105Ah Essential Heated card ChatGPT showed. Panbo says the unit is heated but measured no heater current or warm-up. Use it only as evidence that Epoch delivers its rated capacity.

findings.label: Heater trigger conditions (owner quoting the Renogy manual, not measured)
findings.value: Starts below 41°F (5°C), stops above 50°F (10°C), needs a steady charge current above 4 A per battery
findings.source_title: Self Heating, Renogy 12v Smart 100ah Lithium Batteries – Van Living Forum (JamesAdam, post #10, 2021-10-23)
findings.note: Included only to frame the Van Conversion measurement. It agrees with the Renogy manual figures CompareFoundry gives (above 4 A, below 41°F).

findings.label: Warm-up time (LiTime's claim as reported by a review site; no independent measurement found)
findings.value: about 70–90 min from 14°F; about 100–150 min from -4°F; heater needs at least 10 A of charge input
findings.source_title: LiTime 12V 100Ah Self-Heating Review – Solar Power Picks
findings.note: The page says it ran no heater test ('documents real fit, not heater performance testing'). Search snippets of LiTime's own pages give different times (30–60 min from 14°F on one listing, about 90 min on its blog); I didn't open those pages, so treat the spread as unresolved. Use these only as the maker's figure to compare against the Van Conversion measurement.

unsourced: Named-lab or reviewer-measured warm-up time, heater current or cold capacity for the Epoch 12V 105Ah Essential Heated. Searched Panbo, Will Prowse's willapproved.com (lists the heated Epoch V2-T 460Ah as 'cycle tested' but publishes no figures) and retailers.
Will Prowse's heated-battery video measurements. Forum threads mention the video but give no figures, and diysolarforum.com returned 403.

A search snippet from techtest.org gave about 107 Ah / 1,378 Wh for a standard Redodo 100Ah, but I didn't open the page.
